Chapter 12: The Cross and the Gift of Perspective.
You know, it’s so easy to get swept up in the details of daily life—worrying about what’s next, replaying old regrets, or just tackling that never-ending to-do list. But here’s the thing: the cross gives us a whole new way to look at everything. It’s like putting on a pair of glasses that help you see through the lens of grace.
Imagine someone who’s spent years trying to control every little thing. One day, they finally let go. Or think of a person facing disappointment, but instead of getting bitter, they find gratitude for what’s still there. That’s what the cross does—it shifts our focus. Suddenly, it’s not about what we’re missing, but about what we’ve already been given. It gently reminds us: our value isn’t wrapped up in our achievements. It’s anchored in the love that holds us steady.
Most people? They measure success by stuff like money, status, or getting everyone’s approval. The cross, though, calls us to something deeper—a different standard altogether. Faithfulness. Kindness. Humility. It’s a quiet kind of revolution, and it really changes how we show up at work, in our relationships, even how we handle failure.
There are stories of people who, after discovering the message of the cross, began seeing their lives in a whole new light. Picture a business owner choosing integrity over just making a quick profit. Or a student standing up for a friend, even if it means paying a price for it.
Seeing through the perspective of the cross doesn’t mean ignoring what’s really going on. It’s about seeing life more clearly—spotting the beauty tucked inside brokenness, the possibility hiding in every setback. The cross becomes this kind of compass, quietly guiding us toward what matters most.
